gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: He ___ denied knowing anything about the plan (FIRM).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'denied': firmly. Note the doubled m before -ly.

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: The train arrived ___ , despite the snow (PUNCTUAL).
gaps.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'arrived': punctually (-ly). 'Punctuality' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: Club ___ (MEMBER) costs fifty euros a year.
gaps.explanation: "Membership costs" — the fee noun, not the person.

gaps.sentence: Her ___ (JUDGE) of character is rarely wrong.
gaps.explanation: 'Her judgement of character' — the noun follows the possessive.

gaps.sentence: The magazine ___ the politician's words, which caused a scandal (QUOTE).
gaps.hint: quoted wrongly — that is why there was a scandal (mis-)
gaps.explanation: The prefix mis- means wrongly: misquoted explains the scandal. The past tense is needed.

gaps.sentence: There has been a big ___ (IMPROVE) in her tennis.
gaps.explanation: After 'a big' a noun is needed: improvement (-ment noun).
